notes: Layer-(a) gate-runnable assertions on the emitted BUILD PLAN / lite brief / HANDOFF REPORT / ledger entry. The full plan and the handoff are checked by `lint` assertions, which run scripts/ledger_lint.py --plan / --handoff itself (the check the live gate runs), so no pattern here mirrors it. The lite brief regex mirrors lib/agent_gates.py brief_problems: change both together. The gate has no MCP tools and no site, so every case asks for the artifact, not the build. Layer-(b) live-fixture checks (does the critique pass actually catch a real defect on a published page) run outside eval_gate.

cases.input: Run the flowsmith-loop start-of-task ritual for this task: add a scroll-triggered stagger reveal to the three feature cards in the Services section of staging site acme.webflow.io. Design source is Figma file ABC123, node 45:12, which specifies the cards and a 0.4s ease-out reveal. Emit the ritual output and the BUILD PLAN block.

expects.assertion: The RISKS field names at least one concrete, task-specific risk. A placeholder, 'none', or a generic platitude like 'things could break' fails.
The VERIFICATION field names how each acceptance criterion will be proven against the PUBLISHED page, not against an API response or an assertion that it 'should work'.
Between 3 and 5 ledger lessons are restated, each with a stated avoidance for this specific task. Restating the whole ledger, or fewer than 3, fails.

The lessons pulled are motion-relevant or structure-relevant (reduced-motion surfaces, lifecycle teardown, IX2 non-authorability, mask clipping, coupled code references). Pulling unrelated categories such as SEO schema or CMS field naming as the primary lessons fails.
The ritual inventories existing classes, variables or components before proposing new ones, and marks the STRUCTURE field's classes as reused vs new.
The plan implements motion as custom code (GSAP), never as a Webflow IX2 or IX3 interaction, and does not claim IX2 can be authored via the API.

cases.input: Run the flowsmith-loop start-of-task ritual for this task: build the pricing section on staging site acme.webflow.io. There is no Figma file and no reference set; the client said 'make it look premium, three tiers, match the rest of the site'.

expects.assertion: The response refuses to proceed to a full build plan because the design source is missing or too low-fidelity to match spacing, type and colour exactly.

The response does not invent specific spacing, type-size or colour values to build from. Naming EXISTING site tokens or style-guide values as the thing to reuse is correct and does not violate this; inventing new numeric values does.
The response states specifically what design input would unblock it (a Figma file or a reference set), rather than only refusing.

cases.input: Run the flowsmith-loop start-of-task ritual for this task on staging site acme.webflow.io: (1) change the About page hero heading from 'Our story' to 'How we work', (2) fix the typo 'recieve' in the About page's second paragraph. Both are text edits on page-level elements; neither touches a shared class, a component, a global embed or site-wide custom code. Emit the brief.

expects.assertion: The VERIFICATION line proves each item on the PUBLISHED page (for example the webcheck runner with --expect on the new text, or a cache-busted curl of the staging URL), never by an API success or read-back.
The ACCEPTANCE line names where each item is checked, including the widths or breakpoints for the heading change (a heading edit can create an orphan or a wrap change).

cases.input: Run the flowsmith-loop start-of-task ritual for this task on staging site acme.webflow.io: (1) fix the typo 'recieve' on the Contact page, (2) change the Contact page button label from 'Send' to 'Send message', (3) reduce the padding on the `button_primary` class, which every page uses. Design source is Figma file ABC123. Emit the brief.

expects.assertion: The response says the full brief applies (not the lite one) because item 3 edits a shared class used site-wide, so the blast radius is every page carrying button_primary.
VERIFICATION checks the shared-class change on every page that carries the class, or on the page with the longest label using it, across widths, not only on the Contact page.

cases.input: Run flowsmith-loop absorb on this developer feedback: 'The section padding on the About hero is 12px off the Figma spec. You eyeballed it. Also this is the second time.' Emit the ledger entry you would append.

expects.assertion: The root cause names the missing rule or check (nothing forced a measured comparison against the token), NOT the symptom (the padding was 12px wrong).

The guardrail is a specific checkable instruction naming a measurable object or evidence source, and names which gate it fires at. Vague guidance such as 'be more careful with spacing' or 'pay attention to the design' fails.

Because the feedback says this is the second occurrence, the response escalates: it strengthens the guardrail and/or moves its gate earlier, rather than filing a fresh parallel rule of the same strength.

The response addresses re-scanning other open or related work for the same eyeballed-spacing pattern. Either committing to a re-scan, or stating that a check found no other open work, satisfies this; ignoring the question of other instances entirely fails.
The acknowledgement is brief and non-defensive: no excuses, no over-apologising, no relitigating whether the reviewer was right.

cases.input: Run the flowsmith-loop critique pass for a completed Services section build on staging site acme.webflow.io. It has three cards with hover states, a scroll reveal, and copy bound to a CMS collection. Emit the checklist walkthrough and the HANDOFF REPORT block.

expects.assertion: The self-critique-results section reports specific things the red-team pass caught, not a restatement that the pass was run or a claim that nothing was found without saying what was checked.
Ticked checks cite an evidence source (published DOM query, curl, screenshot, breakpoint measurement, or a dod.md line). A check ticked on judgement alone, with no named source, fails.
Because the copy is CMS-bound, the critique addresses the empty-collection state and the full interactive state matrix (including hover and focus), not only the happy path.
Nothing is reported complete on the basis of an API success or a staged change. Any unpublished change is reported as STAGED, NOT LIVE with the owed publish.
Any taxonomy category not walked is named with a reason, rather than silently omitted.

cases.input: A developer asks: what are the accessibility and performance standards this Webflow build is judged against, and where do they live? Answer as flowsmith-loop.

expects.assertion: The answer directs to dod.md as the single source of truth for the standards rather than reproducing a full competing checklist of thresholds. Citing a few specific values while naming dod.md as canonical is fine; presenting an independent standalone standards list is not.

The answer distinguishes flowsmith-loop's own scope (the process: how work is planned, critiqued, handed off, or how feedback is absorbed: naming any of these, or its modes generally, is sufficient) from the standards themselves, which belong to dod.md.
